http://www.jpost.com/travel/article-9029.text: Lithuania is one of my favorite countries in the world. I keep coming back, and every visit uncovers another charming town, fascinating story, or hidden gem - many of which I've shared on the GoTravel website. It's remarkably green, considerably more affordable than many of its Western European neighbors, and offers a welcome escape from the Israeli summer heat.There's another reason to plan your visit carefully. On the last Sunday of every month, dozens of museums, castles, and national heritage sites across Lithuania offer free admission. It's an easy way to save dozens of euros while exploring some of the country's most impressive cultural landmarks.1. Gediminas Tower, VilniusVisible from nearly every corner of the city, Gediminas Tower - together with a surviving section of the old defensive wall - is all that remains of the fortress that once protected medieval Vilnius. It makes an ideal first stop, whether you take the funicular from the northern side or take the short walking trail from the south. Inside, the tower presents engaging historical exhibits, while the hilltop rewards visitors with sweeping panoramic views of the Lithuanian capital.Money saved: €8.2. Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania, VilniusJust a short walk away lies Cathedral Square and the Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania. Just south of the palace lies Pilies Street - literally "Castle Street" - the Old Town's main pedestrian thoroughfare. The reconstructed palace traces the history of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania through grand ceremonial halls, archaeological discoveries, and thoughtfully curated exhibitions.Money saved: €6–10.3. Bastion of the Vilnius Defence WallAfter exploring Vilnius' atmospheric Old Town, the Gate of Dawn, and the nearby market, continue on to one of the city's best-preserved fortifications: The Bastion of the Vilnius Defence Wall. The site features underground tunnels and exhibitions that explore the city's military past.Money saved: €6.4. Energy and Technology Museum, VilniusDirectly across the river from Gediminas Tower is an interactive museum housed in Vilnius' first municipal power plant, built in 1903. The museum combines the original industrial machinery and architecture with hands-on exhibits covering energy, engineering, transport, and technology, making it an engaging visit for both adults and children.Money saved: €9.5. National Gallery of Art, VilniusArt enthusiasts should also make time for the National Gallery of Art, located a short distance away. As Lithuania's leading museum of modern and contemporary art, it showcases paintings, sculptures, photography, prints, installations, and video works that trace the evolution of Lithuanian artistic expression.Money saved: €8.6. Trakai CastleAround 30 minutes from Vilnius stands Trakai Castle, the iconic island fortress set amid the waters of Lake Galvė and one of Lithuania's most recognizable landmarks. While you're there, consider taking a boat trip among the lake's many small islands. On the last Sunday of every month, admission to the castle museum is free.Money saved: €12.7. Open-Air Museum of LithuaniaOn the drive to Kaunas, Lithuania's second-largest city, it's worth stopping at the Open-Air Museum of Lithuania near the shores of the Kaunas Reservoir. The museum stands on the site connected to the former town of Rumšiškės, whose residents were relocated after the reservoir was created. Today, it is one of Europe's largest open-air museums, featuring dozens of traditional wooden homes, farmsteads, windmills, and churches relocated from every region of Lithuania.Money saved: €12.8. Ninth Fort, near KaunasThe Ninth Fort is one of eight defensive forts constructed around Kaunas in the late 19th century. It is best known for its tragic role during the Holocaust, when tens of thousands of people - most of them Lithuanian Jews, along with deportees from other European countries - were imprisoned and murdered there.Today, the site houses a museum with exhibitions covering the Soviet and Nazi occupations, as well as the Holocaust, alongside a monumental memorial considered one of Europe's most striking Holocaust monuments. On the last Sunday of every month, admission to the museum and its exhibitions is free, although guided tours of the underground sections require advance booking and an additional fee.Money saved: €8.The final stop may be a sobering one, but the journey back between Lithuania's two largest cities - just an hour and a half through forests, fields, and seemingly endless greenery - serves as a reminder of why this country leaves such a lasting impression. It is a landscape that refreshes the senses long after the trip has ended.About the author:Carmit Weiss is the director of the GoTravel travel website, one of the most comprehensive and trusted Hebrew-language resources for travelers exploring destinations around the world.

https://www.politico.eu/article/uk-rolls.text: LONDON — Britain is rolling out the royal treatment for Volodymyr Zelenskyy again. King Charles is set to receive the Ukrainian president for an audience as Kyiv faces renewed tensions with Donald Trump’s White House. It is the latest in a series of meetings where the monarch has sought to champion the Ukrainian leader at a critical moment. Zelenskyy said in an X post Wednesday he would meet the king and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham during a visit to the U.K. Advertisement Advertisement Charles hosted Zelenskyy at Sandringham in March 2025, days after Trump and Vice President JD Vance publicly berated the Ukrainian leader in the Oval Office, and at Windsor Castle earlier this year after Ukraine, the U.K., France and Germany published a joint statement calling for a “just and lasting” deal to end the war with Russia. Zelenskyy will get a ceremonial guard from No.12 Company The Irish Guards when he arrives at Downing Street Wednesday afternoon, which a No. 10 spokesperson said is believed to be unprecedented. The latest visit comes amid fresh strains over Trump’s approach to Russia and Ukraine, after he criticized Zelenskyy’s leadership and struck a deal with Moscow to lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports. It will be the first visit to a European capital by the Ukrainian president since Trump made the announcement last Friday, and his second meeting with Burnham. Burnham has so far refused to condemn the U.S. president for making a deal with Russia, telling MPs Wednesday he wants to “try and repair bridges so that the support comes back.” In an overnight statement issued by No. 10 ahead of the visit, Burnham said: “Our rock-solid support to Ukraine is vital for keeping us safe here in the UK and ensuring those on the frontlines have the equipment they need to push back Russia. Advertisement Advertisement “My message to the Ukrainian people could not be clearer, we are with you for as long as it takes, and we will go further and faster in our support to back your courageous fight for peace in Europe. It is not just the right thing to do, but it’s the necessary thing to do. Russia’s aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on our continent.” Downing Street said the U.K. prime minister has asked ministers to draw up proposals for further sanctions, military aid, and fiscal packages to support Ukraine in the coming weeks. Britain will deliver £45 million of surface-to-air missiles and implement a ban on Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports. Britain will also accelerate deliveries of more than 5,000 Lightweight Multirole Missiles to Ukraine over the next four years with £1.6 billion in funding, Downing Street said.
